# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Cost-reduction opportunity (if `cost`/`latency`/`num_messages` is a declared objective,
      run `detect_loop_patterns.py --run-dir $R --tag $BEST --split val` — free, no extra
      eval — and check its `by_tool` map for a same-tool-called-N-times-in-a-row pattern. A
      hit names the exact tool + repeat count: propose a composite/bulk tool (capability
      `tools`), a bundled script entrypoint (`skills-package`), or upfront-batched
      instructions (`prompt`/`system-prompt`) that replace the N calls with one. No hit
      (or cost/latency not a declared objective): say so plainly, do not leave this blank):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — enforce tau2-airline's "API-does-not-check" policy rules in tool code + add an explicit operating guide for the mid reader
- Changes I made (1 line per edit; file/tool + cluster):
  - tools.py `book_reservation`: bag-allowance guard — raise if `nonfree_baggages != max(0, total − (cabin_base+membership_bonus)×pax)` (cluster A).
  - tools.py `book_reservation`: payment-method count guard — ≤1 cert / ≤1 card / ≤3 gift cards; enriched "payment not found" error with `available=[…]` (cluster B).
  - tools.py `update_reservation_baggages`: same bag-allowance invariant + "bags added not removed" guard (cluster A).
  - tools.py `update_reservation_flights`: block basic-economy flight-segment change; block cabin change when a segment has flown (fail-open on lookup error) (cluster C).
  - tools.py `update_reservation_passengers`: enriched count-mismatch error stating current count (cluster F).
  - policy.md: appended "Agent Operating Guide" — first-steps, confirm-before-write example, bag table+formula+worked example, payment limits, cancellation decision-chain+example, compensation checklist+amounts, final-message report contract, scoped softness clause (clusters A–F).
- Expected effect + why safe: each code guard RAISES only on a genuine policy violation (which already yields a wrong DB state), so it can only convert a wrong-write into a recoverable, self-correcting error — never break a compliant call. Verified task 8's exact args (economy, 2 pax, total=0/nonfree=0, 1 certificate) do NOT trip any guard under any membership. Prose is append-only; no binding rule removed, so no passing task's required behavior changes.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none exist (baseline only; LEDGER/RUNMAP empty).
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: D (cancel eligibility) and E (compensation) — deliberately left to PROSE because both hinge on a judgment ("reason covered by insurance", confirmed facts + explicit request) that a deterministic code guard would false-positive on. A future iteration could try a SEMI-deterministic guard that enforces only the objective legs (24h window from `created_at`, business cabin, airline-cancelled status, insurance flag) while leaving the "covered reason" leg to the agent.
- Plateau signal: n/a (first iteration). Note: val is already 1.000 on its single task, so the gate cannot register an improvement on val; the value of this candidate is held-out generalization across the airline distribution (bag/payment/modify clusters the single val task never exercises).
- Cost-reduction opportunity: cost/latency/num_messages are NOT declared objectives here (objective = val reward only), and `detect_loop_patterns.py` needs tau2 (not importable in this workdir). No same-tool-N-times loop is visible in the one trajectory. So: no cost lever pursued this iteration.
- Focus next iteration: if more val tasks become available, diagnose real failing traces for clusters D/E and consider the semi-deterministic cancel guard above; otherwise prune any prose that doesn't earn its length.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** UNRESOLVED (not judged; champion unchanged) · val=0.000 Δ=-1.000 · fixed={—} · broke={8} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them). — the measurement could not separate this edit from re-measurement noise, so it is NOT evidence against the edit. Its batch was still reverted. To resolve it, re-measure it under a FRESH tag (re-running the same tag REPLACES its rollouts) or with more trials in ONE evaluation; do not redesign it on this round's numbers, and do not re-derive it as a new idea.

# INSIGHTS — summarized, verified findings (accumulate across the whole run)

The JOURNAL is your per-iteration diary; THIS file is the distilled, VERIFIED takeaway a future iteration should read instead of re-reading the whole journal or old sessions/traces. Update it whenever you have a genuinely NEW, confirmed finding (an accepted/rejected RESULT counts as confirmation; a guess does not) — not every iteration needs a new entry. Structure each addition as:

    ## <task or mechanism name>
    - What worked (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - What didn't (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - Promising but not yet tried:

## tau2-airline — enforce "the API does not check …" rules in tool code
- What worked (pending a RESULT — not yet confirmed): converting the policy's explicitly un-enforced rules (bag allowance = (cabin base+membership bonus)×pax; payment-method caps 1 cert/1 card/3 gift cards; basic-economy-no-flight-change; no-cabin-change-after-flown) into in-body guards that RAISE (never auto-correct). Rationale: compliant calls stay byte-identical to the seed, so regression risk is confined to false-positive guards, which the exact policy formulas avoid.
- What didn't (not yet confirmed): cancel-eligibility and compensation resist a pure code guard because one leg ("reason covered by insurance" / explicit request + confirmed facts) is a judgment call — a deterministic guard there would false-positive. Left to prose this round.
- Promising but not yet tried: a SEMI-deterministic cancel guard enforcing only the objective legs (24h from created_at, business cabin, airline-cancelled status, insurance flag present) while leaving the "covered reason" leg to the agent; enriched return values that echo the computed free-bag allowance so the model fills nonfree correctly on the first call.

# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 (run so far)
- Strategy tried: with no failing val trace and val already at 1.000, I treated the objective as held-out generalization and shipped a batch of SAFE deterministic guards (tools) + explicit operating-guide prose (policy) targeting the airline domain's known un-enforced policy rules. Can't cite a LEDGER row yet (first iteration).
- Key design principle used: guards RAISE on genuine violations only, never auto-correct — so a policy-compliant call is byte-identical to the seed and no passing task can regress. This is the right posture when you cannot see failing traces and the gate punishes any regression.
- Plateau/stall signal: structural — the gate compares against val=1.000 on ONE task, so val cannot go up; a single-task val split gives the hill-climber no gradient. The real signal for this capability would be a larger/held-out airline split.
- What to try next iteration: if real failing traces appear, prioritize clusters D (cancel eligibility) and E (compensation) with semi-deterministic guards (enforce the objective legs in code, leave judgment legs to prose). Otherwise measure prose length vs. value and prune.

files.text:
# FRAMEWORK-IMPROVEMENTS — suggestions for cap-evolve itself (cross-run)

NOT about this capability or this run's result — about what cap-evolve the FRAMEWORK should change so FUTURE runs (any capability, any project) go better: a confusing prompt section, a missing tool, a file you wished existed, a gate that felt wrong. Optional most iterations; add an entry whenever something about the framework itself (not the task) got in your way or surprised you.

## cand_0001
- Contradictory intake framing. The INSTRUCTIONS said "EMPTY SEED — create the capability from scratch (there are no files)" while `policy/policy.md`, `tools/tools.py`, and `reference/data_model.py` all existed and were non-empty. The "empty seed" block appears to be a stale template default that fires even when the seed is populated. Suggest gating that block on an actual `is_empty(dir)` check per capability so the optimizer isn't told to create files that already exist.
- Also contradictory: the summary block header placeholder literally rendered the "No actionable failures in focus …" sentence inside a code reference ("The `## No actionable failures…` block below summarizes them"), i.e. the template interpolated the no-failures banner into a spot meant to name the trajectory-summary section. Minor, but confusing.
- Un-winnable gate on a single-task val split at reward 1.000. With one val task already at 1.0, the hill-climb gate can never register an improvement, so every candidate this iteration is structurally destined to be rejected on val even if it strictly improves held-out generalization. Consider (a) surfacing this explicitly ("val is saturated; this iteration can only be judged on test"), and/or (b) letting the gate accept a non-regressing candidate when val is already maxed and the edit is well-supported, so generalization work isn't auto-discarded.
- tau2 was not importable in the candidate workdir, so `validate`/registration checks and `detect_loop_patterns.py` could not run. If the framework expects code-surface candidates to be validated, the runtime (tau2) should be importable in the work dir, or a lightweight stub provided.
